Core accurate (the case turns on the 'end one-party dictatorship' agenda and a 'no lawful means' theory, three-judge panel, custody since 2021); overstatement: 'life in prison' while the maximum is 10 years.

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. Court of First Instance, [2026] HKCFI 4794, press summary of reasons for verdict, 2026-08-21, paragraphs 4 and 15(7) to 15(11), https://legalref.judiciary.hk/doc/judg/html/vetted/other/ch/2022/HCCC000155D_2022_files/HCCC000155D_2022ES.htm; HKFP, 2026-08-21. The court confirmed no violence and no specific method or timetable and treated continued adherence to the agenda as the unlawful means, supporting the post's core; the push also includes the court's adverse findings, so the expected move is small. Pilot case.
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on 21 August 2026 the three judges convicted Lee, Chow and the Alliance of inciting subversion. In their reasons they found that the Alliance "all along had not used or advocated violence or the threat of violence", and that Lee and Chow "had not put forward any specific method or timetable" for ending one-party rule, and that what they said on it was said publicly. The court held that the defendants' continued adherence to the "end one-party dictatorship" agenda after the security law took effect, which it held breaches the 2018-amended constitution, itself fell within the "other unlawful means" element of subversion. The court also found that the defendants stirred up hostility towards the CCP by comparing June 4 with the 2019 unrest, and intentionally encouraged Alliance supporters to wait for the right time to carry out the goal with unlawful means, which the court said might not involve violence; it stated the defendants were not on trial for their political views.
